detail.body:
## Overview

GLM-5.3-Flash can now take metadata-only image and video inputs in Python EPD, the same out-of-band placeholder path as Qwen-VL (#50390) and audio models (#57887). The encoder publishes `image_grid_thw`, and for video `video_grid_thw` plus one timestamp per temporal patch. The consumer rebuilds placeholders from those fields and receives embeddings through the EC connector.

No open PR covers this. #61418 is routing-metadata adapters, not EPD media metadata.

## Claims

- An EC consumer no longer reruns GLM-5.3-Flash vision preprocessing when the encoder published the placeholder metadata.
- On a cold 1E+1PD pair this is about 1.14× request throughput and 0.86× TTFT versus forwarding the raw image. The same ratio holds after each arm has warmed its own CUDA graphs.
- On 32 greedy image requests and 16 greedy video requests, prompt token counts and answer text matched the raw-media path on every request. Image and video throughput are separate tables. The image ratio above is not a video result.

## Validation

Not a duplicate of an open PR (search above).

AI assistance was used. The submitting human should review the diff.

Parser contract on the same H200 pod, against the installed tree with this patch (`pytest` 9.1.1, `torchvision` 0.28.0):

```bash
python3 -m pytest -q tests/models/glm5next/test_epd_metadata.py
```

4 passed in 15.54s.

End-to-end on 8× H200, `zai-org` checkpoint `/models/GLM-5.3-Flash` (bf16/fp8), vLLM 0.32.0 plus this patch. The PD worker loads the full checkpoint, 76.5 GiB per TP=4 rank, so the PD side is TP=4 on GPU 4–7. The encoder is a dedicated `ec_producer` and runs encoder-only. In the throughput runs it was also started at TP=4 on GPU 0–3, and each encoder worker loaded 1.17 GiB; a later startup of this patch with `--tensor-parallel-size 1` loaded 1.93 GiB and used 4579 MiB on one GPU. Encoder TP=4 was not required for the vision tower. `ECExampleConnector` over local disk was used because `ECMooncakeConnector` producers require `tensor_parallel_size=1`, and the producer was originally launched with the full-model command. That check does not rule out Mooncake for an encoder-only producer. The tables below were measured with encoder TP=4 and `ECExampleConnector`. Max model len 8192, prefix caching left on for the PD instance, CUDA graphs on, concurrency 64, 64 distinct 768×768 images, 64 output tokens, greedy. Each arm was a fresh process start plus one warmup request, then two measured passes. Zero failed requests. The metadata proxy logged 129 rewrites; the raw proxy (`--no-rewrite`) logged 0.

| arm | pass | req/s | output tok/s | mean TTFT | mean TPOT |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| raw | cold | 5.46 | 349 | 7575 ms | 59.0 ms |
| raw | warm | 10.91 | 698 | 3573 ms | 31.0 ms |
| metadata-only | cold | 6.22 | 398 | 6530 ms | 50.1 ms |
| metadata-only | warm | 12.51 | 800 | 3076 ms | 26.9 ms |

Logs: the run was on a private pod; the table is the `Serving Benchmark Result` block from `vllm bench serve`.

Video throughput was rerun with `vllm bench serve` after the first 16-request burst proved to be one unschedulable wave (raw warm slower than raw cold, metadata cold dominated by a few multi-second prefills). This run is a different pod, same image and patch. Each arm is a fresh 1E+1PD process and a fresh EC cache. 64 distinct 2-second 320×240 clips at 8 fps, ShareGPT dataset, 64 output tokens, greedy, concurrency 8. One probe measured 248 prompt tokens, and 8192 / 248 caps concurrency at 8. Pass 1 is preceded by 8 warmups of the first clip so Triton JIT is outside the measurement. Pass 2 and pass 3 are repeats with no extra warmup. Zero failed requests. Mean TTFT stays next to the median, and P99 TTFT stays within about 1.5× the mean. The metadata proxy logged 201 rewrites; the raw proxy logged 0. On each paired pass, metadata-only is slightly ahead (about 1.07–1.11× output tok/s and 0.86–0.92× mean TTFT). Repeating a warm pass on the same arm moves output tok/s by 9–12%, which is the same size as that gap, so this table is not a video speedup claim.

| arm | pass | req/s | output tok/s | mean TTFT | mean TPOT |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| raw | 1 | 4.82 | 308 | 849 ms | 12.8 ms |
| raw | 2 | 6.81 | 436 | 562 ms | 9.7 ms |
| raw | 3 | 6.01 | 385 | 673 ms | 10.4 ms |
| metadata-only | 1 | 5.18 | 331 | 780 ms | 12.1 ms |
| metadata-only | 2 | 7.35 | 471 | 481 ms | 9.6 ms |
| metadata-only | 3 | 6.69 | 428 | 581 ms | 9.7 ms |

Correctness used the same 1E+1PD stack and checkpoint, greedy, `max_tokens=32`, one request at a time. Raw (`--no-rewrite`) first, then metadata-only.

Image: 32 distinct 768×768 images. The metadata proxy logged 32 rewrites.

| image | prompt tokens | answer text |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| match | 32/32 | 32/32 |

Video: 16 distinct 2-second 320×240 clips (8 fps). The metadata proxy logged 16 rewrites. The throughput table above is a separate 64-clip `vllm bench serve` run, not this greedy check.

| video | prompt tokens | answer text |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| match | 16/16 | 16/16 |

Image and video placeholder reconstruction, without a serving stack, is `test_glm5_metadata_only_roundtrip` in `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_glm5next.py`. On the H200 pod, with this patch and the local `/models/GLM-5.3-Flash` processor:

```bash
python3 -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/models/multimodal/processing \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_glm5next.py \
  -k test_glm5_metadata_only_roundtrip -q
```

2 passed in 24.56s (`image` and `video`). Each case builds the prompt from raw media, publishes the EC metadata, and checks that metadata-only inputs reproduce the same prompt token ids and placeholders.

## Details

`Glm4vMultiModalDataParser.embedding_fields` marks the grid and video timestamps as placeholder metadata and the embeds as values, so `allow_missing_mm_embeddings` drops only the embeds on an EC consumer. Timestamps are computed with the existing GLM-5.3 frame sampler and stored on the processed video item, which is what the encoder publishes and what the prompt replacement reads. Image replacement was already grid-sized; it now works when the request carries only `image_grid_thw`.

Video still needs those timestamps because a GLM placeholder includes one timestamp string per temporal patch, not only `grid.prod()`. Requests that omit the metadata stay on the raw-media path.

+class Glm4vMultiModalDataParser(MultiModalDataParser):
+    """Placeholder metadata shared by GLM-4V and GLM-5.3-Flash.
+

+    timestamp string per temporal patch, so those timestamps travel with the
+    grid when embeddings arrive through the EC connector.
+    """

+    embedding_fields = {
+        "image": {"image_embeds": "values", "image_grid_thw": "metadata"},
+        "video": {
+            "video_embeds": "values",
+            "video_grid_thw": "metadata",
+            "timestamps": "metadata",
+        },
+    }
+
+    def __init__(self, spatial_merge_size: int, *args, **kwargs):
+        self._spatial_merge_size = spatial_merge_size
+        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    def _embed_row_count(self, grid_thw: torch.Tensor) -> int:
+        grid = grid_thw
+        if grid.ndim == 1:
+            grid = grid.unsqueeze(0)

+            raise ValueError(

> ECExampleConnector over local disk, not Mooncake: ECMooncakeConnector producers require tensor_parallel_size=1, and this checkpoint does not fit one H200.

Would you mind sharing the encoder launch command? My understanding is that a dedicated ec_producer automatically enables encoder-only mode. In our TP=1 test on latest main, the vision weights were ~1.05 GiB and startup GPU memory was ~3.97 GiB without eager mode. Could you clarify why encoder TP=4 was needed here?

@gty111 
Encoder launch command for the image run:

```
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve /models/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}' \
  --port 19534 \
  --ec-transfer-config '{"ec_connector":"ECExampleConnector","ec_role":"ec_producer","ec_connector_extra_config":{"shared_storage_path":"/ygr-sc/bench-glm53-epd-metadata/ec_cache"}}'

```
No separate `--mm-encoder-only` flag. The video throughput run used the same command except `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":1}'`.

Your reading of current main is right. A dedicated `ec_producer` turned this process into encoder-only mode. The encoder log says "this instance runs the multi-modal encoder only". TP=4 was not required for the encoder. We set it because `ECMooncakeConnector` requires the producer to use `tensor_parallel_size=1`, and at the time we were still treating the producer like a full-model server. The full GLM-5.3-Flash checkpoint does not fit one H200, so both sides were launched with `ECExampleConnector` at TP=4. The 76.46 GiB/rank figure is the PD worker, which is why the PD side stays at TP=4.

I reran the encoder alone on the current patch with `--tensor-parallel-size 1` and `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":1}'`, same otherwise as the command above. It became healthy as encoder-only. Model loading took 1.93 GiB, and the process used 4579 MiB on that one GPU. That is the same range as the ~1.05 GiB vision weights and ~3.97 GiB startup you measured. The published image and video throughput numbers were still measured with the TP=4 encoder above; this TP=1 run is a startup check, not a new throughput table.
